body.p: He has a tent. He has a wife. He has a child, a boy. They three live in the tent. There is a neighbourâs tent. Neighbourâs tent â is of mouse-oldman. The mouse-oldman has a wife. He has a daugther. The son of the bird-oldman keeps coming all the time to the daugther of the mouse-oldman and plaits her hair. And if they plait his hair, then the son of the bird-oldman comes to the daughter of the mouse-oldman by night, as well. The bird-oldman sees his son, and he goes to the mouse-oldman to do the matchmaking. Finally he took her away. The children have moved away, they live together. They live like so, until the snow comes. The bird-oldman says: It seems, I'm going to freeze. I will freeze. Where is my land? The summer passed, and I will fly away, it seemsâ. Mouse-oldman (says): âWhat are you going to do with your son and daughterâ? âHow can she reach my land? If she had wings, she would flyâ. âOur children have started to live togetherâ. âWho would separate them?â âHow can I carry the child of the mouse-oldman?â âHave to carry her some-how.â The wife of the bird-oldman, being sorry for her son, started to cry. âHow would my child reach that far away land?ââIf she had wings, she would fly.â âI wonât let my child go.â âWhy canât the son of the bird-oldman (his child) be left here? âLet him try for one year.â âPerhaps he does not die.â The bird-oldman says: âAll right, my son would stay.â âLet him stay on the plain.â âIt is cold-cold-cold, tomorrow we are leaving.â In the morning, the bird-oldman left, and he left his son. In autumn, the son of the bird-oldman and the daughter of mouse-oldman sleep together. She awoke. The son of the bird-oldman is still sleeping. So he is sleeping, but his wife is stronger. The daughter of the mouse nibbled at him, gnawed him clean.why is the girl in lative?NEE059709
